_comment: Single source of truth for the About page on BOTH platforms. Windows reads it directly; build-apk.sh stages it into Android assets. Static facts only — live version numbers are read from the running device so they can never drift.

items.label: Project
items.value: A personal browser for Windows and Android, built from scratch on top of existing browser engines.
items.note: Repo: github.com/bmbell23/WebForge · issues are the source of truth for all work.

items.label: Nothing is forked
items.value: We did NOT fork Chromium or any browser.
items.note: A Chromium fork means ~100 GB checkouts, multi-hour builds, a Windows build machine, and re-merging upstream forever. Instead each platform consumes a maintained engine as a dependency, and 'following upstream' is a version bump we do deliberately.

items.label: Versioning
items.value: version.txt at the repo root is the single source of truth; the gvc shell function bumps, commits and tags.
items.note: Both apps stamp their build from it. The Windows build injects it via electron-builder extraMetadata; Android derives versionCode as major*10000 + minor*100 + patch.

items.label: Distribution
items.value: Self-hosted on dockerhost over Tailscale — no app stores involved.
items.note: nginx:alpine serves /releases on port 8012. Both apps check it and update themselves in place.

items.label: Sync service
items.value: A ~90-line stdlib-only Python HTTP service (python:3.12-alpine) on port 8013.
items.note: A last-write-wins JSON store carrying bookmarks, Persona definitions and open tabs. Offline-first by design: every client renders its local copy and syncs opportunistically with a 5s timeout, so being off the tailnet never blocks or loses anything. Saved logins are deliberately NOT synced — that needs end-to-end encryption first.

items.label: How tabs sync
items.value: Devices publish per-URL facts — when a URL was opened, when it was closed — rather than a snapshot of what's open.
items.note: A snapshot cannot tell 'closed on the other device' apart from 'opened here while that device was offline'. With facts, a URL is open iff its open stamp beats every tombstone for it, which reconciles correctly after either device has been off the tailnet. Tombstones expire after 30 days.

items.label: Data storage
items.value: Everything is local to the device.
items.note: Bookmarks, settings, hotkeys as JSON. On Windows, credentials and the session live in an AES-256-GCM vault whose key is derived from your master password with scrypt (N=2^15) and exists only in memory while unlocked.

items.label: Personas
items.value: Named workspaces — Personal, Work, and so on — each owning its own set of tabs.
items.note: URL rules route tabs automatically, so a work link opens in Work without being told. Anything no rule claims lands in the built-in Unassigned Persona, which keeps the real ones clean. Definitions sync across devices; which Persona is currently showing is per-device.

items.label: Matching rules
items.value: Three syntaxes, identical wherever you type them: prefix, glob with *, or regex between slashes.
items.note: Anchored at the start and open-ended at the end, so a rule for a site covers everything under it. Persona rules and tab groups share one matcher, so a pattern behaves the same in both places. A malformed pattern matches nothing rather than breaking routing.

items.label: Keyboard
items.value: Ctrl+Space is a leader key: press it, then a key.
items.note: Digits switch Persona; letters jump to that Persona's bound URL, opening it if it isn't already there. Bindings are per-Persona, so the same letter can mean different sites in Work and Personal. Bare single-key shortcuts were tried first and proved far too fragile.

items.label: Tabs follow you
items.value: Open a tab on one device and it appears on the other; close it and it closes there too.
items.note: With three exceptions that are resurrected rather than closed: the tab you are literally looking at, pinned tabs, and hotkey tabs. Tabs bucket into groups by site when a host has more than one open.

items.label: Bookmarks
items.value: Shared across both devices, organized in folders, editable from either one.
items.note: Imported wholesale from Firefox. The local copy is always what gets rendered, so bookmarks work with no network at all.

items.label: Engine
items.value: Chromium, bundled via Electron.
items.note: Electron tracks Chromium stable within weeks. Upgrading the browser engine = bumping the Electron dependency.

items.label: Architecture
items.value: One BaseWindow holding a chrome WebContentsView (the sidebar + nav bar UI) plus one WebContentsView per tab.
items.note: Only the active tab's view is attached. The chrome UI is a dumb renderer of state broadcast from the main process. WebForge's own pages (Settings, Bookmark manager, New tab, this page) are real tabs loaded from local files with a separate privileged preload; web content never gets that bridge.

items.label: Ad blocking
items.value: @ghostery/adblocker-electron with the full prebuilt list set (EasyList, EasyPrivacy, uBlock lists incl. Annoyances), plus extra cosmetic rules for fandom.com.
items.note: The compiled engine is cached in userData, so blocking keeps working offline.

items.label: Auto-update
items.value: electron-updater, generic HTTP provider pointed at the dockerhost release server.
items.note: Differential updates via blockmap — a typical update transfers about 1 MB rather than the full ~83 MB installer.

items.label: How it's built
items.value: electron-builder produces an NSIS installer, cross-built on a Linux server.
items.note: The host has no wine, which electron-builder needs to stamp Windows exe metadata, so the build runs inside the official electronuserland/builder:wine Docker image. Electron and NSIS downloads are cached on the host. Script: scripts/build-windows.sh

items.label: Not code-signed
items.value: The installer is unsigned, so SmartScreen warns on first run.
items.note: Expected for a self-hosted personal build; a code-signing certificate would remove it.

items.label: Engine
items.value: Android System WebView — Chromium, kept up to date by the OS through Google Play.
items.note: The engine updates itself independently of this app, so the browser core stays current with no work on our side. GeckoView was considered and deferred; it would be revisited only if WebView proves too limiting.

items.label: Architecture
items.value: A native Kotlin shell (single Activity, no UI frameworks or third-party dependencies) hosting one WebView per tab.
items.note: Only the active tab is attached to the view tree. Drawn edge-to-edge: the status bar sits above a padded strip in the bar colour, and the gesture navigation bar stays visible so you can still swipe out of the app.

items.label: One bar, at the top
items.value: Tabs on the left, address in the middle, bookmarks on the right — mirroring the two Windows sidebars.
items.note: Panels are dismissed by swiping, pages reload by pulling down, and settings live behind the gear on the bookmarks page. Bookmarks are edited in place with drag handles and folders.

items.label: Feature parity
items.value: Personas, Persona routing rules, tab groups, bookmark editing and cross-device tab sync all work the same as on Windows.
items.note: The matching and tab-sync logic are deliberate ports of the Windows implementations, kept in step so both devices agree. The master-password vault and ad blocking are Windows-only so far.

items.label: Dependencies
items.value: None. The app uses only the Android framework and Kotlin's standard library.
items.note: Deliberate — it keeps the APK tiny (well under 1 MB) and the build hermetic.

items.label: Self-update
items.value: On resume, the app compares its version against the release server and offers the newer APK.
items.note: Downloaded with DownloadManager and handed to the system installer. The signing key stays constant, so Android treats it as an upgrade rather than requiring an uninstall.

items.label: How it's built
items.value: Gradle + Android Gradle Plugin, built on the Linux server; the APK and version endpoint are staged to the release server.
items.note: Script: scripts/build-apk.sh

items.label: Android SDK
items.value: compile 34 · target 34 · min 26 (Android 8.0)
